| [A6: Recoverable Knowledge and the Permission to Inquire](A6-recoverable-knowledge-v01.md) | 2,634 | Explicit conditions make higher-order knowledge recoverable from every finite evidential history. | Sufficient-condition proof and abstract countermodel; philosophical significance and originality remain open. |

These articles develop A4 and A6 from Claude's ambitious selection. They preserve the prior review's distinction between a promising topic and an achieved contribution. No existing essay, dossier, selection, final submission, or orchestrator status was overwritten. No new pipeline code was created.

The user's suggestion to broaden review beyond the judge panel is implemented in the adversarial review. Relevant published arguments determine the objections; imagined authority supplies no evidence. The “future reviewer” standard is used to ask what a better-informed critic could disprove, not to manufacture a confidence score.

## Source record

The main targets were read in the repository's extracted texts: Andreas and Günther's *A Regularity Theory of Causation*, especially §§2 and 5, and Carter and Hawthorne's *Dogmatism & Inquiry*, especially §§4.1–4.2. These were supplied by the existing research workflow, not reconstructed from bibliographic titles.

Further sources actually consulted:

- Gallow, *A Model-Invariant Theory of Causation* (2021), model-invariance discussion: https://pgrim.org/philosophersannual/41articles/gallow-amodel.pdf. Author publication list confirms volume and pages: https://jdmitrigallow.com/papers/.
- Brown, *Knowledge, Inquiry and Dogmatism* (2025), especially §3: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11229-025-05008-4.
- Fiat, *Knowing to Infinity: Full Knowledge and the Margin-for-Error Principle* (2025), introduction and relevant discussions of epistemic interests and full knowledge: https://yonathanfiat.com/assets/pdf/Knowing%20to%20infinity%20final.pdf.
- Carter and Hawthorne's published metadata: *Mind* 133 (531), 651–676, DOI https://doi.org/10.1093/mind/fzad070. The draft's section references concern the inspected author manuscript.

**New unresolved source request:** Douglas Ehring, “Preemption, Direct Causation, and Identity,” *Synthese* 85 (1990): 55–70, DOI https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00873194. The author's PDF route returned a retrieval error twice: https://people.smu.edu/dehring/files/2022/03/33.-Preemption-Direct-Causation-and-Identity-1990.pdf. Metadata was verified, but the argument has not been read; a search snippet is only a reason to obtain it. Its treatment of dense causal chains may defeat the proposed increment of A4. A copy of the full paper is needed before clearing originality.

Other source requests already recorded for different candidates remain in the earlier review. The six PDFs the user previously supplied were reassessed there and must not be requested again.

## Development priorities

For A4, determine whether the formal observation has an admissible realization under the exact regularity account, and read Ehring before claiming novelty. For A6, assess whether the proved local-recovery result changes a live philosophical argument enough to warrant an article. Independent assessment may reasonably demote either draft.

The current lengths are deliberately below 6,000 words. The earlier request to bring existing essays 4 and 5 to the limit does not justify padding these new candidates before their contributions survive review. Expansion should add an argument, a decisive comparison, or a defensible application.

## Process and provenance

The user asked the assistant to help Claude draft articles, authorized publication to GitHub in the existing session, and supplied a methodological suggestion about adversarial review. The user explicitly withheld philosophical feedback for the contest. No philosophical feedback was requested for these drafts. No other models or delegated agents were run during their production.

The prior [provenance notice](../ambitious-review-20261022/PROVENANCE.md) remains in force. This session is not represented as an isolated, clean-origin contest-authoring run. These files are external working drafts. They do not certify compliance of a final entry, resume the contest orchestrator, or erase the previously reported exposure concern. No unrelated personal philosophical material is used as a premise or reproduced in these files.

All work in this packet is new writing for review. The bibliography entries identify the sources of attributed views; the main formal observations are presented with proofs and without a claim of first discovery. Source-access gaps and failed research directions are recorded openly rather than converted into positive novelty verdicts.
